claims.text: Adding 5–10 at.% Cr and/or Al to a refractory high-entropy alloy promotes formation of a continuous oxide scale.
The oxide scale formed after Cr and/or Al addition is adherent.
The protective scale consists primarily of Cr2O3 and/or Al2O3.
A continuous Cr2O3 and/or Al2O3 scale retards oxygen diffusion.
Adding 5–10 at.% Cr and/or Al improves the high-temperature oxidation resistance of the refractory high-entropy alloy.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy undergoes significant oxidation weight gain under the proposed exposure conditions.
The untreated alloy experiences oxide-scale spallation under the proposed exposure conditions.
Cr and/or Al oxidizes preferentially at high temperature in the modified alloy.
Preferential oxidation of the added Cr and/or Al forms a stable oxide layer.
The stable oxide layer reduces oxygen ingress into the underlying alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress minimizes further oxidation and degradation.
After 72 hours at approximately 1100 °C in flowing air or controlled oxygen partial pressure, the modified alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
After the specified exposure, the modified alloy will have a more continuous oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
After the specified exposure, the modified alloy will have a more intact oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
